replies.text: Why Nobody Lives in Qazaqstan ? the answer is simple : The Qazaq famine of 1930–1933, also known as the Asharshylyq, was a man-made famine in the Qazaq Autonomous Socialist Soviet Republic, then part of the Bolshevik empire , during which an estimated 1.3 to 2.3 million people died, the majority of them ethnic Qazaqs .Between 38 and 42 percent of all Qazaqs perished, the highest proportion of any ethnic group killed in the Bolshevik famines of the early 1930s. Other estimates put the number of deaths at about 1.75 million, while some research suggests the toll may have exceeded 2 million.
